content.text: CCNA 200-301 STUDY MANUAL
Chapter 7
Layer 2 Switching

This document replaces Chapter 7 of Todd Lammle, CCNA Certification Study Guide, Volume 2, Exam 200-301 (2020), book pages 193 to 218 (PDF pages 251 to 276). It follows the book's order, keeps its learning objectives, and adds plain-English explanations, command breakdowns, labs and questions. Every difference from the book is tagged.
| Item | Detail |
| Book pages | 193 to 218 (PDF page = book page + 58, checked on this chapter) |

| Tracker rows | Chapter 7 - Layer 2 Switching; topics 7.1 and 7.2; subtopics 7.1.1, 7.1.2, 7.2.1, 7.2.2 (7 rows). Seq range: not checked, because the Notion tracker was not connected in this chat CHECK |
| Suggested time | About 5 to 7 hours: 1.5 h reading, 2.5 h labs, 1.5 h questions. A suggestion, not a measured need. |
| Exam versions | v1.1 (retires 2 Feb 2027) and v2.0 (starts 3 Feb 2027). |
| Status of your knowledge | Not assessed. |
Tag legend
| Tag | Meaning |
| BOOK | Taken from the book (page given where useful). |
| UPDATED | The book is outdated, wrong or unclear. The text says what changed and why. |
| ADDED | Extra material that is not in the chapter. |
| CHECK | Not verified on real equipment or not confirmed in an official source. |
WHAT THE BOOK SAYS

Learning objectives from the book (v1.0 numbers): 1.13 Describe switching concepts: 1.13.a MAC learning and aging, 1.13.b Frame switching, 1.13.c Frame flooding, 1.13.d MAC address table. 5.7 Configure Layer 2 security features (DHCP snooping, dynamic ARP inspection, and port security). This chapter covers the port security part of 5.7.
VERIFY

Verification note. The MAC learning, flooding and forwarding examples, the management subnet 192.168.10.16/28, the multicast-MAC test and the MAC-address format checks were calculated or simulated with a Python script. Nothing was run on real Cisco equipment. Outputs not copied from the book are marked CHECK .

| 7.1.2 Port security | 5.7 | 4.7.e Port security (inside 4.7 Configure Layer 2 security features) | High |

| Storm control (not in the book) ADDED | Not listed | 4.7.c Storm control | Medium for v2.0 |
UPDATED / MODERN NOTE

The v2.0 outline was read directly from Cisco's PDF. Cisco says related topics may still appear, so MAC learning stays worth knowing. v1.1 objective numbers come from the book and secondary sources CHECK .
Write your answers first, then mark confidence: K (know), U (unsure), G (guessed). Answers are in Answer Key A.
Q1. A switch receives a unicast frame. The destination MAC is not in its MAC table. What does it do? (K / U / G)
Q2. What are the default maximum MAC addresses and the default violation mode when port security is enabled? (K / U / G)
Q3. Which violation mode drops the offending frames but sends no log message or SNMP trap? (K / U / G)
Q4. On which interface do you put the management IP address of a Layer 2 switch? (K / U / G)
Q5. What is the default MAC address aging time on a Catalyst switch? (K / U / G)

The idea in plain words. A Layer 2 switch reads the MAC address in each Ethernet frame and decides: send it out one port, or send it out many. It does not read the IP header, so it is fast. Each switch port is its own collision domain, but by default the whole switch is still one broadcast domain. BOOK pp194-195
- Hardware-based (ASICs), wire speed, low latency, low cost. BOOK
- A switch is like a multiport bridge. Old bridges used software; switches use ASICs for the MAC table. BOOK
- The switch does not change the packet. It only reads the frame, which is why it is faster than a router. BOOK
UPDATED / MODERN NOTE

The book calls the MAC table the "forward/filter table" and says CAM is its "old name". Cisco's current command and term is MAC address table (show mac address-table). CAM (content addressable memory) is the hardware memory type, and people still say "CAM table". UPDATED
7.1.1 Three Switch Functions at Layer 2
| Function | What it means |
| Address learning | The switch records the source MAC of every frame and the port it came in on. |
| Forward / filter decision | It looks up the destination MAC. Known: send only out that port (filter). Unknown or broadcast: flood. |
| Loop avoidance | Redundant links make loops. Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) blocks some ports. Covered in Chapter 9. |
Address learning, step by step [BOOK]
At power-on the MAC table is empty. The switch learns only from source addresses. BOOK pp195-197
- Host A sends a frame to Host B. The switch learns A's MAC on port Fa0/0.
- B's MAC is unknown, so the switch floods the frame out every port except Fa0/0.
- B replies. The switch learns B's MAC on Fa0/1.
- Now A and B talk directly. The switch filters: only those two ports carry the frames.
- Hosts C and D that have not sent anything are not in the table yet.
VERIFY

I simulated this in Python with a four-port switch. Results: (1) A to B with an empty table: flood out Fa0/1, Fa0/2, Fa0/3. (2) B to A: forward out Fa0/0. (3) A to B again: forward out Fa0/1 only. (4) A broadcast (ffff.ffff.ffff): flood out all ports except the source. (5) A to unknown host C: flood. The source MAC is always learned first. ADDED
The book's table example [BOOK]

The book shows a table with 000a.f467.9e8c on Fa0/3 and asks what happens to a frame from 0005.dccb.d74b to 000a.f467.9e8c. Answer (script checked): the destination is known, so the frame goes only out Fa0/3. If the destination were not in the table, it would be flooded out all ports except the one it came in on. BOOK p198
Format of the MAC address table (two entries from the book's example) BOOK
Switch# show mac address-table
Vlan Mac Address Type Ports
1 0005.dccb.d74b DYNAMIC Fa0/1
1 000a.f467.9e8c DYNAMIC Fa0/3
- Vlan - MAC addresses are kept per VLAN.
- Mac Address - the learned source MAC, in Cisco format (three groups of four hex digits).
- Type - DYNAMIC was learned; STATIC was typed in or built in.
- Ports - the port where that MAC was last seen.
Aging [ADDED]

If a MAC is not heard from for a while, the switch deletes it. The default aging time is 300 seconds (5 minutes), changed with mac address-table aging-time. The book only says "a certain time period". ADDED Source: secondary (Cisco course material copy); CHECK on your device.
COMMON MISTAKE
The book's sample outputs contain a garbled header: Ports]]>. That is a print error and is not part of the command output. UPDATED
WARNING

Frame flooding triggers: unknown unicast, broadcast, and (without extra features) multicast. Flooding is normal, but too much of it is a sign of a table problem or an attack (a MAC flooding attack tries to fill the table so the switch floods everything). ADDED CHECK
Loop avoidance: the problems [BOOK]

Redundant links are good, but without STP they cause: broadcast storms (frames loop forever), multiple copies of one frame at a device, MAC table thrashing (the same MAC seems to move between ports), and loops inside loops. STP solves all of these. The book leaves the details to Chapter 9. BOOK pp202-204
Quick check 7.1.1
Q1. A frame arrives on Fa0/2. The destination MAC is unknown. What does the switch do?
Answer: Floods it out all ports except Fa0/2 - It also learns the source MAC on Fa0/2 first.
Q2. Does a switch learn from the source or the destination MAC?
Answer: Source - The destination is only used for the lookup.
Q3. How many broadcast domains does a default switch have?
Answer: One - Each port is a separate collision domain.
Q4. Name two problems STP prevents.
Answer: Broadcast storms and MAC table thrashing (also multiple frame copies) - All three come from loops.
7.1.2 Port Security

By default any device can plug into a switch port and its MAC will be learned. Port security limits which MAC addresses may use a port, and sets a penalty if the rule is broken. It stops a stranger plugging in a laptop, hub or access point. BOOK pp199-202
MEMORY TIP
Easy security win from the book: shut down unused ports (or move them to an unused VLAN). All ports are enabled by default.
Steps to configure
Typical port-security setup BOOK CHECK
Switch(config)# interface fastEthernet 0/1
Switch(config-if)# switchport mode access
Switch(config-if)# switchport port-security
Switch(config-if)# switchport port-security maximum 2
Switch(config-if)# switchport port-security mac-address sticky
Switch(config-if)# switchport port-security violation shutdown
- switchport mode access - makes the port a fixed access port. Port security does not work on a port still in dynamic mode.
- switchport port-security - turns the feature on. The other commands set values but do nothing until this one is entered.
- maximum 2 - allow up to 2 MAC addresses on this port. Default is 1.
- mac-address sticky - learn MACs dynamically and save them as if they were typed in. They go in the running-config; use copy running-config startup-config to keep them after a reload.
- violation shutdown - what to do when a rule is broken (see the next table). Shutdown is the default.
Violation modes [BOOK]
| Mode | Drops offending frames | Log message and counter | SNMP trap | Port state |
| protect | Yes | No | No | Stays up |
| restrict | Yes | Yes | Yes | Stays up |
| shutdown (default) | Yes (port off) | Yes | Yes | err-disabled |
VERIFY

Protect has no log or trap; restrict and shutdown do. This matches the book's review question 5 and a Cisco Community post. The default of 1 MAC and shutdown matches a Cisco Catalyst 6500 configuration guide (an older official guide). Source type: mostly secondary. CHECK
Recovering an err-disabled port
Manual recovery BOOK CHECK
Switch(config)# interface fastEthernet 0/1
Switch(config-if)# shutdown
Switch(config-if)# no shutdown
Remove the cause first (the extra device), or the port will fail again. Automatic recovery is possible with errdisable recovery cause psecure-violation (and an interval). ADDED CHECK
The lobby PC example [BOOK]
Allow only one known PC, and do not shut the port when someone else plugs in BOOK UPDATED
Switch(config-if)# switchport port-security
Switch(config-if)# switchport port-security violation restrict
Switch(config-if)# switchport port-security mac-address aabb.ccdd.eeff
COMMON MISTAKE

The book types the MAC as aa.bb.cc.dd.ee.ff. IOS wants the Cisco format: three groups of four hex digits, like aabb.ccdd.eeff. My format check confirmed aa.bb.cc.dd.ee.ff is not valid, while aabb.ccdd.eeff and the book's 00C0.35F0.8301 are valid. UPDATED
The book's verification output on p212 shows Last Source Address:Vlan : 0013:0ca69:00bb3:00ba8:1, which is not a valid MAC. That is a print error. UPDATED
COMMON MISTAKE
Three places where the book contradicts itself or is out of date:

(1) p200 says most Cisco switches ship with ports in dynamic desirable mode. On the 2960, 3560, 3650 and 3850 the default is dynamic auto; desirable was the default on old 2950/3550 models. UPDATED (Cisco Community answers; secondary.)

(2) p200 says port security cannot be configured on a dynamic port, and p211 says the port must be access or trunk. Both agree that dynamic mode is not allowed; the exam answer is: make it an access port first. UPDATED

(3) p210 says a secure port can hold 1 to 8,192 MAC addresses and the 3560 supports 6,144. The allowed maximum depends on the switch model and IOS; other sources show 3,072 or 6,272. Do not memorise a number. UPDATED CHECK
Verify port security [BOOK]
Verification commands BOOK
Switch# show port-security
Switch# show port-security interface fastEthernet 0/1
Switch# show running-config
Shape of the output (illustrative, shortened) CHECK
Port Security : Enabled
Port Status : Secure-up
Violation Mode : Shutdown
Maximum MAC Addresses : 1
Total MAC Addresses : 1
Sticky MAC Addresses : 0
Security Violation Count : 0
- Port Security : Enabled - the feature is on. The book shows a port where Disabled appears even though a violation mode was set. Setting values does not enable it.
- Port Status - Secure-down (no host yet), Secure-up (working), Secure-shutdown (violation, the port is err-disabled).
- Maximum / Total MAC Addresses - the limit and how many have been learned.
- Security Violation Count - how many violations happened.
EXAM CRITICAL

Port security facts to remember: off by default; when on, defaults are max 1 and violation shutdown; port must be access (not dynamic); sticky saves learned MACs; switchport port-security must be entered for anything to work.
Quick check 7.1.2
Q1. You set violation restrict on a port but never typed switchport port-security. Is port security working?
Answer: No - The feature is off until that command is entered.
Q2. Maximum is 2, sticky is on. A third MAC appears and the mode is the default. What happens?
Answer: The port goes err-disabled (shutdown) - Script check of the logic: m1, m2 learned, m3 is a violation.
Q3. Which two violation modes send an SNMP trap?
Answer: restrict and shutdown - Protect sends nothing.
Q4. How do you bring back an err-disabled secure port by hand?
Answer: shutdown, then no shutdown on the interface - After removing the cause.

The book builds a small network of three switches (S1, S2, S3), each linked to the others with two cables. It covers: administrative setup, a management IP address and subnet mask, the default gateway, port security, and testing. BOOK pp204-206
UPDATED / MODERN NOTE
The book's hardware (2960, 3560, 3850, console on the back, PoE button on the front) is dated; current Catalyst 9000 switches run IOS XE. The commands in this chapter are the same. UPDATED
7.2.1 Catalyst Switch Configuration
Cables, link lights and Spanning Tree [BOOK]
- The book says switch-to-switch links need a crossover cable unless the switch autodetects, and adds: "in the Cisco exam objectives, switches never autodetect". BOOK p206

- Update: auto-MDIX (automatic crossover detection) has been on by default on Catalyst switches since IOS 12.2(18)SE, and Gigabit Ethernet includes it. On real modern gear, straight-through cables work between switches. Treat the book's rule as an exam-style rule only if a question states it. UPDATED (Cisco course material copy and a Cisco Community post; secondary.) CHECK

- Link lights go amber, then green while spanning tree converges. The book says this takes about 50 seconds. For a newly connected port with classic STP it is typically 30 seconds (15 listening plus 15 learning); 50 seconds is the figure that includes the 20-second max-age wait after an indirect failure. Newer switches default to Rapid PVST+, which is much faster. UPDATED CHECK (general knowledge of IEEE 802.1D timers; not looked up)
- Alternating green and amber on a port LED means errors; check the NIC, the cable and the duplex setting. BOOK CHECK
Does a switch need an IP address? [BOOK]

No. A switch switches frames with no IP address. You add one only for management: Telnet, SSH and SNMP need an IP address to reach the switch. The address goes on a logical interface, normally interface vlan 1 (an SVI, switch virtual interface). Cisco recommends using a different VLAN than VLAN 1 for management. BOOK pp206-207
EXAM CRITICAL
No IP address on physical switch ports in a Layer 2 switch, no routing protocol. The management IP is on a VLAN interface (SVI). There is no AUX port on Cisco switches. BOOK p207
Core of the book's S1 configuration BOOK CHECK
Switch> enable
Switch# configure terminal
Switch(config)# hostname S1
S1(config)# enable secret todd
S1(config)# interface vlan 1
S1(config-if)# no shutdown
S1(config-if)# exit
S1(config)# ip default-gateway 192.168.10.30
S1(config)# end
S1# copy running-config startup-config
- hostname S1 - names the device.
- enable secret todd - encrypted password for privileged mode (a weak password, used only in the lab).
- interface vlan 1 - the management SVI.

- ip address 192.168.10.17 255.255.255.240 - management address. Script check: 192.168.10.16/28 has usable hosts .17 to .30 (14 hosts) and broadcast .31, so .17, .18, .19 (S1, S2, S3) and the gateway .30 are all valid.
- no shutdown - the SVI is shut down by default. The book stresses this on p212.

- ip default-gateway 192.168.10.30 - lets you manage the switch from other subnets. It uses the last usable address in this book example. It is for a Layer 2 switch (if ip routing is on, the switch ignores it). ADDED CHECK
- copy running-config startup-config - saves the configuration.
COMMON MISTAKE

Errors in the book's S2 configuration (p207-208): S2 sets an IP on interface vlan 1 but never types no shutdown, yet the book then pings successfully from S2. On a real switch S2's SVI would stay down. Add no shutdown. The book also names one switch SW-3 in a prompt. UPDATED
The first ping shows .!!!! (80 percent). The book explains the first loss is ARP resolving the MAC address. That is correct. BOOK
UPDATED / MODERN NOTE

Security update. The book uses password console, password telnet, login and Telnet. Telnet sends passwords in clear text. Today use SSH with a local user. The v2.0 outline (4.1) lists local usernames. UPDATED Sketch below, not tested: CHECK
SSH instead of Telnet ADDED CHECK
S1(config)# ip domain-name lab.local
S1(config)# username admin secret StrongPass1
S1(config)# crypto key generate rsa modulus 2048
S1(config)# ip ssh version 2
S1(config)# line vty 0 15
S1(config-line)# transport input ssh
S1(config-line)# login local
- ip domain-name and crypto key generate rsa - needed to create SSH keys (hostname must also be set).
- username admin secret ... - a local account with an encrypted password.
- transport input ssh - only SSH is accepted on the virtual lines.
- login local - check the local username database.
Port security in the lab [BOOK]

The book enables port security on S3 ports Fa0/3 and Fa0/4 (one device each) with interface range f0/3-4, switchport mode access, switchport port-security. It then shows show port-security interface f0/3 with default values: Violation Mode Shutdown, Maximum 1, Port Status Secure-down (no host plugged in yet). BOOK pp210-212
- interface range f0/3-4 - applies the next commands to both ports at once.
- On Fa0/6 the book sets only violation restrict. The output shows Port Security: Disabled, proving values alone do nothing.
WHAT THE BOOK SAYS

The book says some switches show err-disabled while others show Secure-shutdown, and that there is no difference. Both describe the same condition. show interfaces status shows err-disabled; show port-security interface shows Secure-shutdown. BOOK CHECK
Quick check 7.2.1
Q1. On which interface do you put the management IP of a Layer 2 switch?
Answer: A VLAN interface (SVI), usually interface vlan 1 - Not on a physical port.
Q2. You set an IP on interface vlan 1 and the interface shows administratively down. Why?
Answer: The SVI is shut down by default; type no shutdown - A very common mistake.
Q3. Why did the first ping lose one packet?
Answer: ARP had to resolve the MAC address first - The later pings work.
Q4. Is a default gateway needed on a switch?
Answer: Only to manage it from another subnet - Switching itself does not need it.
7.2.2 Verifying Cisco Catalyst Switches
| Command | What it shows |
| show running-config | The whole configuration (large). Good first overview. |
| show interface vlan 1 (or show ip interface brief) | Is the management SVI up/up, and which IP it has. |
| show mac address-table | The MAC table: learned (DYNAMIC) and STATIC entries. |
| show ip arp | IP to MAC mappings the switch has learned. A dash in the Age column marks the switch's own address. |
| show port-security / show port-security interface | Port security settings and status. |
Book example (shortened) BOOK
S3# show interface vlan 1
Vlan1 is up, line protocol is up
Hardware is EtherSVI, address is ecc8.8202.82c0
Internet address is 192.168.10.19/28
- Vlan1 is up, line protocol is up - the SVI works. If it says administratively down, type no shutdown.
- Internet address ... /28 - confirm the management IP and mask.
Reading the book's MAC table output [BOOK]

- The first line, All 0100.0ccc.cccc STATIC CPU, is not the switch's base MAC address as the book says. It is a multicast MAC used by Cisco protocols such as CDP, VTP, DTP and UDLD, so frames sent to it go to the switch CPU. My script confirms the first byte 01 marks it as a group (multicast) address. Cisco's Catalyst best-practice document (official) lists 01-00-0c-cc-cc-cc for CDP. UPDATED
- Six MACs on Fa0/1 means a switch (or hub) is behind that port: many MACs on one port. BOOK
- S2's table shows seven MACs on Fa0/5, and none on Fa0/6. The book says STP put Fa0/6 into blocking (the redundant link to S3). That is correct reasoning. BOOK
Static MAC address [BOOK]
Permanent entry (command form) BOOK CHECK
S3(config)# mac address-table static aaaa.bbbb.cccc vlan 1 interface fastEthernet 0/7
- mac address-table static - creates a permanent entry; it does not age out.
- aaaa.bbbb.cccc vlan 1 - the MAC and the VLAN it applies to.
- interface fastEthernet 0/7 - where frames for that MAC are sent.
COMMON MISTAKE

The book's output for this step shows aaaa.bbbb.0ccc instead of aaaa.bbbb.cccc. That is a typo in the book. Typing static MACs for all hosts is a lot of work; use sticky port security instead. UPDATED
Quick check 7.2.2
Q1. Which command shows IP to MAC mappings?
Answer: show ip arp - ARP table.
Q2. What does STATIC CPU for 0100.0ccc.cccc mean?
Answer: A built-in multicast MAC for Cisco control protocols; frames go to the switch CPU - It is not the base MAC.
Q3. Many MACs are learned on one port. What is probably behind it?
Answer: Another switch or hub - Many devices share that port.
Q4. Type of entry created by mac address-table static?
Answer: STATIC (permanent) - It does not age out.
The book has no troubleshooting section here, so this section is added. ADDED CHECK (not tested on hardware)
| Symptom | Likely cause | First check |
| Cannot ping or Telnet/SSH to the switch | SVI shut down, wrong IP/mask, no default gateway (from another subnet), wrong VLAN | show ip interface brief; show interface vlan 1 |
| A port went down by itself | Port security violation (err-disabled) | show interfaces status; show port-security interface |
| Port security is configured but does not block | switchport port-security was never entered | show port-security interface (Port Security: Disabled) |
| Cannot enable port security | Port is in dynamic mode | Type switchport mode access first |
| Legitimate new PC blocked | Max is 1 and the old MAC is stuck (sticky or static) | show port-security address; raise max or clear the old MAC |
| Link up/up but slow, many errors | Duplex or speed mismatch, bad cable | show interfaces counters; check duplex and speed on both ends |
| Frames flood everywhere | Entries aged out, MAC table full, loop or attack | show mac address-table count; check STP (Chapter 9) |
| Host is in the wrong place in the MAC table | Loop or flapping MAC between ports | Log messages about MAC flapping; check STP |
| Topic | Remember |
| Three functions | Address learning, forward/filter, loop avoidance (STP). |
| Learning | From the SOURCE MAC, per VLAN, into the MAC address table. |
| Forwarding | Known destination: out that port only. Unknown unicast or broadcast: flood out all ports except the incoming one. |
| Domains | Each port = collision domain. Switch = one broadcast domain until VLANs. |
| Aging | Default 300 seconds. Static entries do not age. |
| Show | show mac address-table, show ip arp, show interface vlan 1, show port-security. |
| Port security defaults | Off by default. When on: max 1 MAC, violation shutdown. |
| Prerequisite | Access mode first, then switchport port-security. |
| Violation modes | protect: drop, no log. restrict: drop + log + SNMP. shutdown: err-disabled + log + SNMP. |
| Sticky | Learns MACs and saves them to running-config. |
| Recover | shutdown then no shutdown. |
| Management IP | On the SVI (interface vlan 1), no shutdown, plus ip default-gateway for remote access. |
| Unused ports | Shut them down or move to an unused VLAN. |
| Remote access | Prefer SSH to Telnet. |

sections.title: How far this has been tested

content.text: VERIFY
Nothing in this document was run on real Cisco hardware or in Packet Tracer. Try every command in your own lab and record what you saw.

Use Cisco Packet Tracer with 2960 switches and PCs. Simulator output may differ from real switches. Write down what you actually saw, including mistakes, in the self-assessment table and in your tracker.
- Build one switch (SW1) with PC1 on Fa0/1, PC2 on Fa0/2 and PC3 on Fa0/3. Addresses: PC1 192.168.10.1, PC2 192.168.10.2, PC3 192.168.10.3, all /24 (switch has no IP).
- On SW1 run show mac address-table. Expected: no entries for the PCs yet (only built-in entries, possibly). CHECK

- From PC1 ping PC2. Run show mac address-table again. Expected: the MACs of PC1 (Fa0/1) and PC2 (Fa0/2) appear as DYNAMIC. PC3 does not appear, because it has sent no frame. Why: the switch learns only from source addresses. CHECK
- Run show mac address-table aging-time. Expected: 300 seconds by default. CHECK
- Run clear mac address-table dynamic, then show the table. Expected: the dynamic entries are gone and return after new traffic. CHECK
- Add a static entry: mac address-table static 0001.0001.0001 vlan 1 interface fastEthernet 0/3. Expected: a STATIC entry on Fa0/3. CHECK
Secure Fa0/1 with sticky learning CHECK
SW1(config)# interface fastEthernet 0/1
SW1(config-if)# switchport mode access
SW1(config-if)# switchport port-security
SW1(config-if)# switchport port-security maximum 1
SW1(config-if)# switchport port-security mac-address sticky
SW1(config-if)# switchport port-security violation shutdown
- Enter the commands above. Run show port-security interface fastEthernet 0/1. Expected: Port Security Enabled, Maximum 1, Violation Mode Shutdown. CHECK
- Ping from PC1 through Fa0/1. Run show running-config interface fastEthernet 0/1. Expected: a switchport port-security mac-address sticky line with PC1's MAC. CHECK

- Connect a second device behind Fa0/1 (a small switch with PC4, or swap PC1 for another PC) and send traffic. Expected: the port goes err-disabled, the link light goes down, and a log message appears. show port-security interface shows Secure-shutdown and a violation count of 1. CHECK
- Recover: remove the extra device, then shutdown and no shutdown. Expected: the port returns to up/up. CHECK
- Change to violation restrict, repeat step 3. Expected: the port stays up, extra frames are dropped, the violation counter increases. CHECK
- Try switchport port-security on a port left in the default mode. Expected on real Catalyst: an error saying it is a dynamic port. Packet Tracer may behave differently. CHECK
- Connect SW1 to SW2 with a cable. Give SW1 interface vlan 1 192.168.10.17/28 and SW2 192.168.10.18/28, both with no shutdown.
- From SW2: ping 192.168.10.17. Expected: .!!!! with the first ping lost while ARP resolves. Why: ARP. CHECK
- Run show ip arp on SW2. Expected: an entry for 192.168.10.17 and SW2's own address with a dash in the Age column. CHECK

- Configure SSH on SW1 using the SSH sketch above. From a PC in the same subnet (give it 192.168.10.20/28 and gateway 192.168.10.30) use the PC's SSH client. Expected: login with the local user. Packet Tracer may need its own crypto steps. CHECK
- Remove no shutdown from the test by typing shutdown on SW1's vlan 1. Expected: ping fails; show interface vlan 1 shows administratively down. Re-enable it. CHECK

questions.q: A frame arrives on Fa0/2. The destination MAC is unknown. What does the switch do?

questions.q: Name two problems STP prevents.

content.text: Q1 A frame arrives on Fa0/2. The destination MAC is unknown. What does the switch do?
Answer: Floods it out all ports except Fa0/2 - It also learns the source MAC on Fa0/2 first.
Q2 Does a switch learn from the source or the destination MAC?
Answer: Source - The destination is only used for the lookup.
Q3 How many broadcast domains does a default switch have?
Answer: One - Each port is a separate collision domain.
Q4 Name two problems STP prevents.
Answer: B - roadcast storms and MAC table thrashing (also multiple frame copies) - All three come from loops.
Q1 You set violation restrict on a port but never typed switchport port-security. Is port security working?
Answer: No - The feature is off until that command is entered.
Q2 Maximum is 2, sticky is on. A third MAC appears and the mode is the default. What happens?
Answer: The port goes err-disabled (shutdown) - Script check of the logic: m1, m2 learned, m3 is a violation.
Q3 Which two violation modes send an SNMP trap?
Answer: restrict and shutdown - Protect sends nothing.
Q4 How do you bring back an err-disabled secure port by hand?
Answer: shutdown, then no shutdown on the interface - After removing the cause.
Q1 On which interface do you put the management IP of a Layer 2 switch?
Answer: A - VLAN interface (SVI), usually interface vlan 1 - Not on a physical port.
Q2 You set an IP on interface vlan 1 and the interface shows administratively down. Why?
Answer: The SVI is shut down by default; type no shutdown - A very common mistake.
Q3 Why did the first ping lose one packet?
Answer: A - RP had to resolve the MAC address first - The later pings work.
Q4 Is a default gateway needed on a switch?
Answer: Only to manage it from another subnet - Switching itself does not need it.
Q1 Which command shows IP to MAC mappings?
Answer: show ip arp - ARP table.
Q2 What does STATIC CPU for 0100.0ccc.cccc mean?
Answer: A - built-in multicast MAC for Cisco control protocols; frames go to the switch CPU - It is not the base MAC.
Q3 Many MACs are learned on one port. What is probably behind it?
Answer: A - nother switch or hub - Many devices share that port.
Q4 Type of entry created by mac address-table static?
Answer: STATIC (permanent) - It does not age out.
Q1 A switch receives a frame whose destination MAC is in the table on port Fa0/4. The frame came in on Fa0/2. What happens?
Answer: It is forwarded only out Fa0/4 - Known destination means filtering (script checked).
Q2 Same switch, but the destination is not in the table. What happens?
Answer: Flooded out all ports except Fa0/2 - The source is also learned on Fa0/2.
Q3 Which address does a switch learn from?
A. Source MAC
B. Destination MAC
C. Source IP
D. Destination IP
Answer: A - A Layer 2 switch ignores IP.
Q4 How many collision and broadcast domains does an 8-port switch with default settings have?
Answer: 8 collision domains, 1 broadcast domain - Every port is its own collision domain; no VLANs yet.
Q5 What is the default MAC aging time?
Answer: 300 seconds - Secondary source; check on your device. CHECK
Q6 Which three functions does a Layer 2 switch perform?
Answer: A - ddress learning, forward/filter decisions, loop avoidance - The book's three functions.
Q7 Which problem is NOT caused by switching loops?
A. Broadcast storm
B. MAC table thrashing
C. Multiple frame copies
D. Duplicate IP addresses
Answer: D - Duplicate IPs come from addressing mistakes.
Q8 Which command shows the MAC address table?
Answer: show mac address-table - Older IOS uses show mac-address-table.
Q9 What are the defaults after you enable port security on a port?
Answer: Maximum 1 MAC, violation shutdown - Port security itself is off until enabled.
Q10 Which mode does not shut the port and sends no log or SNMP trap?
A. protect
B. restrict
C. shutdown
D. err-disable
Answer: A - Restrict logs and traps; shutdown also disables the port.
Q11 You type switchport port-security on a port still in default dynamic mode. What do you expect?
Answer: The command is rejected; make it an access port first - Port security is not allowed on dynamic ports. CHECK
Q12 Which command makes learned MACs stick to the configuration?
Answer: switchport port-security mac-address sticky - They go in the running-config; save to keep them.
Q13 Maximum is 3, sticky is on, four different PCs connect in turn. What happens to the fourth?
Answer: A - violation; with the default mode the port goes err-disabled - Three MACs fill the limit.
Q14 How do you recover an err-disabled secure port by hand?
Answer: shutdown, then no shutdown - After fixing the cause.
Q15 Is this a valid MAC for IOS: aa.bb.cc.dd.ee.ff?
Answer: No. Use aabb.ccdd.eeff - Format check by script.
Q16 Where do you configure the management IP address on a Layer 2 switch?
Answer: On an SVI, for example interface vlan 1 - Not on a physical port.
Q17 You set an SVI IP address but cannot ping it. The interface is administratively down. Fix?
Answer: no shutdown on the SVI - SVI is shut down by default.
Q18 Management subnet 192.168.10.16/28. What are the usable host range and a valid gateway at the top of the range?
Answer: 192.168.10.17 to 192.168.10.30; gateway 192.168.10.30 - Broadcast is .31 (script checked).
Q19 Why is Telnet a poor choice for managing a switch?
Answer: It sends passwords in clear text; use SSH - Update to the book. UPDATED
Q20 What does All 0100.0ccc.cccc STATIC CPU mean in the MAC table?
Answer: A - built-in multicast MAC for Cisco protocols like CDP, handled by the CPU - Not the switch base MAC.
Q21 A port shows many learned MACs. What is likely behind it?
Answer: A - nother switch, a hub or an access point - Many hosts share one port.
Q22 (v2.0) Which port-security-related objective number covers Layer 2 security in the v2.0 outline?
Answer: 4.7.e (inside 4.7) - Official v2.0 PDF.
